title: Phase 8 · Stage 25: Shelfwise goes online
summary: Move to a real web host: register the clock, ids, repositories and Library in the dependency injection container, choose lifetimes, and serve the first read-only endpoints.

steps.title: A new front end, the same core
body: The library wants Shelfwise on the web, so a phone app and the front desk can share it. This is where the layers pay for themselves: **Domain, Application and Infrastructure move across unchanged**. Only the top of `Program.cs` is replaced. Instead of a command loop reading stdin, it builds a **web host**.

**This stage starts from a provided port**, not from your stage 24 code (a web program is compiled differently, so the editor cannot carry your console file over). The port is your stage 24 namespaces, unchanged, plus one helper in Infrastructure, `DemoData.Seed(Library)`, which adds three books (The Hobbit, Dune, Emma) and two members (1 Ada Lovelace, Premium; 2 Grace Hopper, Standard). The console commands are gone. From the next step on, the editor carries **your** web code again.

In the console you wired everything by hand at the top. A web host has a **container** that does it for you: you register *what to use for each type*, and it builds the objects (and whatever their constructors ask for) on demand:
builder.Services.AddSingleton<Library>();                                            // the container fills its constructor
app.MapGet("/books", (Library library) => library.Books.Select(BookDto.From));         // asked for by parameter

**Lifetimes** decide how long an object lives: **singleton** (one for the whole app), **scoped** (one per HTTP request), **transient** (a new one every time). The library's state lives in memory, so the clock, ids, repositories and the Library must all be **singletons**, or every request would see an empty library.

steps.prompt: Match each lifetime to what it gives you.
pairs: one instance for the life of the app
a new instance every time one is needed
steps.explain: In-memory state must be a singleton. Scoped suits per-request things like a database session; transient suits small stateless helpers.

steps.prompt: `InMemoryRepository<Book, string>` is registered with `AddTransient`. What happens?
options: Every request gets an empty repository, so added books vanish
It works exactly like a singleton
Books are shared, but members are not
steps.explain: The container builds a fresh repository each time something asks for one, so nothing survives between requests (and the Library, as a singleton, would keep the first one forever: a classic lifetime bug).

steps.prompt: Register the clock so that both `ManualClock` and `IClock` resolve to the same object.
steps.explain: A factory lambda forwards `IClock` to the registered `ManualClock`, so advancing one advances the other.

steps.title: Register the services and list the books
prompt: The editor holds the **provided port** (read its first comment). Keep `/health`. Then:

1. Register, all as **singletons**: one `ManualClock` starting on 2026-03-02 (registered both as itself and as `IClock`, as in the blanks step), `IIdGenerator` as `SequentialIdGenerator`, the three `IRepository<...>` as `InMemoryRepository<...>`, and `Library`.

4. In `namespace Shelfwise.Api` add `public record BookDto(string Isbn, string Title, string Author, int Year, string Genre, int Copies, int Available, string? Shelf)` with `public static BookDto From(Book book)` (the genre as its name, copies = total).
5. `GET /books` returns every book as a `BookDto` in catalog order.
Press **Run checks**: the dojo starts your server and calls it.

template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("the service could be checked", async () =>
Dojo.Eq("GET /health returns ok", "ok", await DojoWeb.Text(await http.GetAsync("/health")));
var root = await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync("/"));
Dojo.Eq("GET / names the service", "Shelfwise", DojoWeb.Prop(root, "name"));
Dojo.Eq("GET / says version 2", "2", DojoWeb.Prop(root, "version"));
await Dojo.TryAsync("GET /books could be checked", async () =>
var r = await http.GetAsync("/books");
DojoWeb.Status("GET /books responds 200 OK", 200, r);
var json = await DojoWeb.Json(r);
Dojo.Eq("GET /books lists the three demo books in order", "978-0261103344,978-0441172719,978-0141439518", Keys(json, "isbn"));
Dojo.Eq("the first book is The Hobbit", "The Hobbit", DojoWeb.Prop(At(json, 0), "title"));
Dojo.Eq("its genre is the name Fiction", "Fiction", DojoWeb.Prop(At(json, 0), "genre"));
Dojo.Eq("it has 3 copies", "3", DojoWeb.Prop(At(json, 0), "copies"));
Dojo.Eq("all 3 are available", "3", DojoWeb.Prop(At(json, 0), "available"));
Dojo.Eq("Emma's genre is General", "General", DojoWeb.Prop(At(json, 2), "genre"));
Dojo.Eq("a second call returns the same books (the repository is a singleton)", "978-0261103344,978-0441172719,978-0141439518", Keys(await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync("/books")), "isbn"));
// "a,b,c" from one property of every item in a JSON array, so one row checks which items came back, in order.
static string Keys(JsonElement json, string property) => json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array
? string.Join(",", json.EnumerateArray().Select(e => DojoWeb.Prop(e, property)))
: "(not a JSON array: " + json.ValueKind + ")";
static JsonElement At(JsonElement json, int index) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && index < json.GetArrayLength() ? json[index] : default;
static JsonElement Get(JsonElement json, string property) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object && json.TryGetProperty(property, out var value) ? value : default;
static async Task<JsonElement> GetJson(HttpClient http, string url) => await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync(url));
static bool IsProblem(HttpResponseMessage r) => r.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType == "application/problem+json";

require.message: Registers the book repository as a singleton

hints: Every registration is one line before `builder.Build()`: `builder.Services.AddSingleton<IRepository<Book, string>, InMemoryRepository<Book, string>>();` and so on. The clock is two lines, as in the blanks step.
The container can build `Library` because every constructor parameter is registered. Seed right after `Build()` with `app.Services.GetRequiredService<Library>()`.

`public static BookDto From(Book book) => new(book.Isbn, book.Title, book.Author, book.Year, book.Genre.ToString(), book.TotalCopies, book.AvailableCopies, book.Shelf);` and `app.MapGet("/books", (Library library) => library.Books.Select(BookDto.From));`.

steps.title: Members, one book, and the clock
prompt: Add, keeping everything from the last step:
| `GET /books/{isbn}` | 200 with the `BookDto`, or **404** when there is no such book |
| `GET /members` | every member as `MemberDto(int Id, string Name, string Email, string Tier, decimal Owes)` |
| `POST /clock/advance?days=3` | moves the `ManualClock` (inject it) and returns `{"today":"2026-03-05"}`; `days` missing or below 1 is **400** |
Add `MemberDto` (with `From(Member member, Money owes)`) to `Shelfwise.Api`. Because the clock is a singleton, `GET /today` after an advance shows the new date.

? string.Join(",", json.EnumerateArray().Select(e => DojoWeb.Prop(e, property)))

json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && index < json.GetArrayLength() ? json[index] : default;

json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object && json.TryGetProperty(property, out var value) ? value : default;

hints: Return `IResult` when an endpoint can answer two ways: `book is null ? Results.NotFound() : Results.Ok(BookDto.From(book))`.
Endpoints can ask for any registered service: `(int? days, ManualClock clock) => ...`. A missing query parameter arrives as `null` when the parameter is nullable.
For the advance: `if (days is not int d || d < 1) return Results.BadRequest(); clock.Advance(d); return Results.Ok(new { today = clock.Today });`.
